quarterly_data.signal: 2025 revenue by product: AOC-brand (own-brand) optoelectronic products NT$1,508,495 thousand (68.72% of revenue, versus NT$1,076,886 thousand or 61.54% in 2024); RF device wafer foundry NT$407,169 thousand (18.55%); optoelectronic device wafer foundry NT$221,769 thousand (10.10%); technical service revenue NT$57,722 thousand (2.63%). quarterly_data.quarter: Global Communication Semiconductors annual report: GCS Holdings 2025 Annual Report (04-05-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: AOC-brand products (GaAs/InGaAs PIN photodiodes, backside-illuminated photodiodes, laser diodes, VCSELs, InGaAs APDs) have been developed and mass-produced for 155 Mbps up to 1,600 Gbps optical communication. Letter: the company continued developing 200G photodiodes and related transmitter components to meet data-center customers' demand for 100G to 1.6T or higher-speed optical transceiver modules, and the PD product line achieved a high market share in 2025 (company claim); it also invested in continuous wave (CW) laser development. The 200G/Lane InGaAs PIN photodetector was successfully developed in 2025; 400G/Lane photodetectors and CW lasers are in development to provide a complete optical chipset, and 70mW and 100mW CW lasers are aimed at silicon-photonics (CPO) modules.
quarterly_data.figure: 200G/Lane InGaAs PIN PD developed in 2025; 400G/Lane PD and 70mW / 100mW CW lasers in development

quarterly_data.quarter: Global Communication Semiconductors annual report: GCS Holdings 2025 Annual Report (04-05-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Outlook for 2026 (letter to shareholders): in its own-brand optoelectronic business the company will maintain the market share of its photodiode products and seek customer qualification and mass-production orders for transmitter components in 2026 to expand its customer base; optoelectronic wafer foundry will focus on foundry services for IDM companies and other mass-production opportunities; RF wafer foundry will focus on improving profitability. Management expects AI-driven cloud capex to be a key growth driver for the optical communication market.

quarterly_data.quarter: Global Communication Semiconductors annual report: GCS Holdings 2025 Annual Report (04-05-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Capacity: the company's primary revenue source relies on its 4-inch wafer fab in California, and capacity constraints have led it to pursue joint ventures and investments to expand capacity. In 2025 its wholly owned subsidiary GCS Device Technologies established an Asia operations center and planned to set up a back-end production line in the Hsinchu Science Park. To expand production capacity, the company participated in the cash capital increase of Wellywave Technology in April 2026, acquiring 60.05% equity; Wellywave is a III-V compound semiconductor foundry service provider.
quarterly_data.figure: 4-inch fab (California); 60.05% of Wellywave Technology acquired April 2026
